Approach (Inez, training) | Requires | Cash | Time | Trail | What it leaves |
Ask cold | Nothing | $0 | 20 s | +1 | A refusal that is remembered. Later offers cost +$10,000 and +1 Trail. |
Pay | A Watch first, where one is offered (20 s, any agent) | $70,000 | 35 s | +2 | A traceable payment. The relationship stays neutral. |
Help (clear her debt) | Need known (Listen, 30 s) | $40,000 | 35 s | +1 | Gratitude. Her bravery can grow. |
Pressure (threaten) | Need known | $0 | 25 s | +3 | Fear. Her resentment grows, and she can identify the Fixer. |
Built The approach prices are proven in play; the Watch time is a starting value. Paying Inez plus turning the driver costs $110,000 against a $100,000 purse. Helping her plus turning the driver costs $80,000. So finding things out is what pays for a second route.
Turning is private. A conversation is private: asking, paying, helping and listening have no witnesses, so onlookers learn nothing, there is no witness Trail, no change in Standing, no incident and nothing passed along. The approach keeps its own price: a payment is still traceable money, and a Loyal person still reports an approach. Pressure is different: security see a threat at any Alert, and ordinary people from Alert 2 (§05); it is remembered and passed on. A conversation never counts as loitering (§05). Spec

The city moves without you › The crowd is cover and witness Spec
Who notices depends on who they are and how high Alert is. Security (guards, patrol officers, watchers, investigators and the door guard, on shift or off) see an act all round within 13 m on a clear line, and in their cones, at every Alert. Ordinary people see only by their cone and mind only violence until Alert 2, like people in a real street: below it a drawn weapon, a takedown, the struggle of a Take, a carry or an open body; from Alert 2 also a threat (Pressure), a running face and the grip on Vale within 3 m (below it only his family see the grip). Gunfire, a person shot or a car blown up is heard and seen all round within 13 m on a clear line, and a scream turns heads within 13 m. Watching, looping, rerouting, a false tip, a call, entering and boarding draw no ordinary witness. A witnessed traceable act adds +1 Trail per incident and moves Standing. Dense crowds also break the sightlines of guards and cameras. Busy streets are both a hiding place and a risk. Turning is private (§04): asking, paying, helping and listening have no witnesses. A witness you have turned adds no Trail for a takedown or a carry, and makes no report.

Temperament | Responds to | If you are Heroes | If you are a Menace |

Knowledge makes consent cheap. Reputation decides who says yes. › Coerced contacts get bitter
Compliant → Resentful → Informer. They rise one step each time you pressure them or they are exposed. An Informer sells a route to the police or rivals, which schedules an ambush in a later mission. Spec
Talkers, not only turncoats. Every person holds facts: who saw the Fixer's face, who saw the Enforcer's (a witness to a takedown, or a victim who saw him coming), who knows the cell's car, who saw where you went and when. A captured agent knows far more: every agent's face, the cell's car, the mission's place and time, and every contact the cell has turned (§08). Someone who reported you volunteers what they saw. Questioned, a person gives up what they know when fear plus resentment outweighs bravery plus loyalty. The rule is fixed, so the same situation always gives the same answer. A contact can stop short of Informer and still fold under questioning. A brave, helped contact lies for you, and investigators get nothing or a false lead. Spec

Knowledge makes consent cheap. Reputation decides who says yes. › Coerced contacts get bitter
Compliant → Resentful → Informer. They rise one step each time you pressure them or they are exposed. An Informer sells a route to the police or rivals, which schedules an ambush in a later mission. Spec
Talkers, not only turncoats. Every person holds facts: who saw the Fixer's face, who saw the Enforcer's (a witness to a takedown, or a victim who saw him coming), who knows the cell's car, who saw where you went and when. A captured agent knows far more: every agent's face, the cell's car, the mission's place and time, and every contact the cell has turned (§08). Someone who reported you volunteers what they saw. Questioned, a person gives up what they know when fear plus resentment outweighs bravery plus loyalty. The rule is fixed, so the same situation always gives the same answer. A contact can stop short of Informer and still fold under questioning. A brave, helped contact lies for you, and investigators get nothing or a false lead. Spec

Knowledge makes consent cheap. Reputation decides who says yes. › Four ways to turn someone
Approach (Inez, training) | Requires | Cash | Time | Trail | What it leaves |
Ask cold | Nothing | $0 | 20 s | +1 | A refusal that is remembered. Later offers cost +$10,000 and +1 Trail. |
Pay | A Watch first, where one is offered (20 s, any agent) | $70,000 | 35 s | +2 | A traceable payment. The relationship stays neutral. |
Help (clear her debt) | Need known (Listen, 30 s) | $40,000 | 35 s | +1 | Gratitude. Her bravery can grow. |
Pressure (threaten) | Need known | $0 | 25 s | +3 | Fear. Her resentment grows, and she can identify the Fixer. |
Built The approach prices are proven in play; the Watch time is a starting value. Paying Inez plus turning the driver costs $110,000 against a $100,000 purse. Helping her plus turning the driver costs $80,000. So finding things out is what pays for a second route.
Turning is private. A conversation is private: asking, paying, helping and listening have no witnesses, so onlookers learn nothing, there is no witness Trail, no change in Standing, no incident and nothing passed along. The approach keeps its own price: a payment is still traceable money, and a Loyal person still reports an approach. Pressure is different: security see a threat at any Alert, and ordinary people from Alert 2 (§05); it is remembered and passed on. A conversation never counts as loitering (§05). Spec

hits.text:
Read the street at a glance › The fail camera and payoff cuts
On a fail , the camera shows the culprit, in the view the player is in, with a caption ("The guard saw the Enforcer.") and a tip ("The guard watches the door."), six words or fewer each. A tip names what to deal with and why, never the order to give, because everyone can be turned more than one way. The fail line says what actually happened (for a seal: police held the car, Go was never given, or Vale hadn't reached it), and the debrief's story agrees with it. A withdrawal has no fail camera.
Payoff cuts. When a plan lands, cut briefly to a street-level camera before returning to the same state. The capstone guarantees one : Inez's call lands and the guard walks off to her. More payoff cuts and the decisive shot come later. Spec

Handover › G · Take the guard Spec
Tech loops the entrance camera (and reroutes the patrol, if the guard's body will be carried into the yard).
Scout watches the guard, his cone and his check-in marks, from beyond his 26 m cone.
Enforcer waits out of the camera's cone and the sweep, more than 3 m from the guard, walks in and knocks him out just after a mark, then leaves him, or carries him out of the door's sight if someone could find him while the cell still needs the door.

Knowledge makes consent cheap. Reputation decides who says yes. › Routines that live Spec
Partners. Two people tied as lovers who meet stop, face each other and stand together instead of passing. Summoned by a call (§07), he walks his usual route and stops at her free side: the first point on a 1.2 m ring round her post, sides first, with nobody within a metre of it. They face each other; he stays 60 s, they hold for 2 s, and he goes. By chance, two lovers who are both out on the street and not on a post, and who come within 8 m of each other on a clear line, each walk to the other's side and stand facing for 20 s, once a mission per pair.

Approach (Inez, training) | Requires | Cash | Time | Trail | What it leaves |
Ask cold | Nothing | $0 | 20 s | +1 | A refusal that is remembered. Later offers cost +$10,000 and +1 Trail. |
Pay | A Watch first, where one is offered (20 s, any agent) | $70,000 | 35 s | +2 | A traceable payment. The relationship stays neutral. |

§10 PRESENTATION › conversation scene
conversation scene [S]: when an agent arrives and begins Listen, Ask, Pay, Help, Pressure, Call or Mislead, the camera cuts to a close shot of the two people and the opening lines play (at most 3 beats: the arrival line, the person's first reply, or for Listen the overheard exchange's first lines; never the reply, the result or the read, which come at landing as bubbles, so the scene can't contradict the outcome). The mission clock pauses while it plays (the player can't move) and the act's seconds run after it, as priced; the scene changes nothing the engine records, so the same seed and orders give the same result with it, skipped or never played. Played from the ground view as from the map: both people set to idle, facing, feet planted where the engine has them; the low shots stand down the architecture cut and the silhouettes. One bubble at a time, up to 3 s each; click or Space advances, Esc or Skip ends it. Kept on screen: the clock with its pause mark, the Alert pill, the bubbles, the Skip keycap. It doesn't play in a fight or at Alert ≥ 2, if either person is down, gone or inside, while another scene plays, or in freeze or target mode. close [S]: with Vale in the cell's hands, on foot or in the car, his absence is noticed at 6:30: a warning, once, for the HUD (at once if he is taken later). At 7:30 a mission still here fails closed-in, and says why: nobody aboard can drive · who holds the car · Vale still on foot · the car free and nobody said Go. A Take under way holds the verdict until it ends.
route A, front door (before 4:50): Scout watches café, listens to Inez (0:50) → Fixer helps Inez ($40,000; she may need it twice) → Tech loops the entrance camera (20 s, runs 2:00, planted so it still runs at the Enter), then reroutes the patrol (optional) → Fixer calls Inez: the guard walks to her side (about 57 s), stays 60 s, walks back = about a 2:54 window, the walk the grid's, never written here [payoff cut] → Enforcer enters (38 s), exits service door with Vale, to car (about 36 s), Board, Go.
route B, the pickup (from 5:10; built today: the one-car way at the end of this line; the rest, the split, is [D], and §07 the getaway's direction changes its end): Scout listens to the driver: he needs cash (30 s) → Fixer turns the driver before 4:40 (Pay $70,000, or Help $40,000): he warns the rivals' lookout off, and once Vale is in he drives him round to the service bay (13 s) and waits there until 7:30 → Scout gives the rival car a false tip (30 s), or it follows Vale's car and its wheelman reaches him first (the tip is in question, §07 rivals) → Tech reroutes the patrol from the cabinet (by about 4:00), so the yard's sweep is away at the pickup → Enforcer takes Vale from the back seat (38 s); the driver steps out and the Enforcer takes the wheel → Scout, Fixer and Tech gather at the cell's car among the posted three → Go on Vale's car: Vale is out, and the posted three spring on the cell's car → the three down the blocker, board, Go (or break the crew). The cell may instead bring its car round behind Vale's (Drive, 28 s) and carry Vale 3.5 m into it: the one-car way.

§07 HANDOVER › the Take
the Take [S]: at Vale's own car with his driver turned, in the service bay, the Take happens inside the car, off-screen, with nothing to witness, and ends with the Enforcer at the wheel: the driver lends the car (§06) [D; built today, the Take ends with Vale still to be carried to the cell's car]. A Take begun before 7:30 holds the driver until it ends. Any other Take has a 5 s struggle onlookers can see. Escorted on foot, Vale looks wrong only to his kin, or to anyone within 3 m who sees the grip.

§07 HANDOVER › getaway
getaway [S]: the getaway car starts in the square's bay. An agent in it can Drive it to one of the mission's car stands: the square's bay, or the service drive behind Vale's car (nose out, once Vale's car is in; on the drive first, it blocks his way and he stops in the road).
